clue.text: Only son entering project

indicators.note: the son goes into the word for project, so entering marks one piece placed inside another

parts.note: to project is to stick out, to jut
S is the standard abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A lone boy getting involved in a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' looks like a noun (a scheme) but is the verb meaning stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs of restriction: 'only a minute' and 'just a minute' are interchangeable.

clue.text: Drive away one's husband following disqualification

indicators.note: the one's-husband pieces come after the disqualification word, so following orders the charade

parts.note: a ban is a disqualification, as from driving
one is the numeral I, and the 's stands for 'is', giving the letters I and S

explanation.surface: A man losing his licence and having his husband drive him away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' tempts a motoring reading alongside disqualification, but it is the definition: chase off.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to send or chase them off, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lower middle

definitions.meaning: read as low-er, something that lows or moos: a male bovine
the centre of a dartboard or target

explanation.surface: Two bare words, apparently a position: lower middle, as in a class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is not the comparative of low but one who lows, as cattle do.
explanation.definitionFit: A bovine male moos, so it is a lower; and the centre of a target is called by the same name in darts.

clue.text: Hard in small unfriendly place of learning

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: the letter for hard sits within the word for unfriendly, so in marks an insertion

parts.note: cool means distant or unfriendly
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A cramped, hostile, tough institution.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy for pupils is the plainest example of an institution where people learn.

clue.text: Dedicated hospital given permission

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital on road signs and maps
allowed means permitted

explanation.surface: A devoted hospital being granted leave to do something.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground consecrated or set apart as sacred is said to be dedicated, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Sweated labour in New York — OK, possibly, if supporting daughter

indicators.note: in a down answer the scrambled letters sit below the daughter, holding her up, so supporting puts them after
possibly says the letters could be another arrangement of themselves

explanation.surface: Someone sweating through hard work in New York, which is fine if it keeps a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges NEWYORKOK into ONKEYWORK, which lies beneath D in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious hard graft is called drudge work, a synonym for sweated labour.

clue.text: Master criminal amusing friend endlessly, in the morning back inside

indicators.note: the reversed morning letters go within the word for amusing, so inside signals insertion

parts.note: fun means amusing, as in 'a fun evening'

indicators.note: back says the morning abbreviation is read in the other direction

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

indicators.note: endlessly says the friend word loses its final letter

parts.note: chum is a friend

explanation.surface: A villain who once had a funny pal, returning inside one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Fu Manchu is Sax Rohmer's villain; 'back' turns the morning abbreviation round before it goes inside, and 'endlessly' trims the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Sax Rohmer's fictional villain is the archetypal evil mastermind of pulp fiction.

clue.text: Pick up telephone of rising Republican

parts.note: to call is to telephone

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means the word of is read upwards

explanation.surface: An instruction to answer the phone from a Republican on the up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up telephone' reads as one instruction, but 'Pick up' alone is the definition. Of turned upward gives FO.
explanation.definitionFit: Collecting someone, as in 'I'll come by for you at eight', is the phrasal sense of picking a person up.

clue.text: Boast about a century in Polish city

indicators.note: the boast word wraps around the other pieces, so about marks a container

parts.note: to crow is to boast
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: Someone bragging about scoring a hundred in a Polish city.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the older English spelling of Kraków.
explanation.definitionFit: Kraków, the old royal capital in southern Poland, has long been spelled this way in English.

clue.text: When one chooses a woven cloth

parts.note: twill is a fabric woven with diagonal ribs

explanation.surface: Choosing a fabric whenever you like.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means as and whenever one wishes, freely by choice.

clue.text: Put one in mind of watch left Eisenhower

parts.note: to look is to watch
Ike was the nickname of US president Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A watch reminding someone of Eisenhower, who left it behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To resemble someone is to remind people of them, so the phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Expecting interfering parents and their children to intervene

indicators.note: the household word comes between the parts of the obstructing phrase, so to intervene marks insertion

parts.note: something interfering is an obstruction, getting in the way
parents and their children make up a family

explanation.surface: Expecting meddling relatives to step in.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a genteel way of saying pregnant, i.e. expecting a baby.

clue.text: Flower in autumn? It's out around end of November

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the last letter of November, so around marks a container
out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: it's is IT IS, written ITS here as fodder letters

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of November

explanation.surface: A query whether a flower blooms in autumn, noting it is out about the end of November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges AUTUMNITS to NASTUTIUM, which goes around R from November.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a garden plant with bright orange and yellow blooms, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Proposed relocation day

parts.note: a move is a relocation to a new home

explanation.surface: A suggested date for moving house.
explanation.definitionFit: In meetings one formally puts forward a motion; having done so, one has proposed it.

clue.text: Expression of incredulity seen originally in a poem

indicators.note: the first letter of seen goes inside the other pieces, so in signals insertion

parts.note: If is a famous poem by Rudyard Kipling

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letter of seen

explanation.surface: Disbelief first spotted in a piece of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's 'If—' is a much-quoted British poem of stoic advice.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a scornful retort meaning 'that's hardly likely', a spoken show of disbelief.

clue.text: Strong wind getting up breaks safety device in part of plane

indicators.note: the storm word splits the safety-device word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a fuse is a safety device in an electrical circuit

indicators.note: in a down answer getting up means the wind word is read upwards

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A rising gale wrecking a safety device in an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' works because this is a down light: the wind is read from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The main body of an aircraft, holding crew and passengers, is one section of the craft.

clue.text: Bird, headless chicken

indicators.note: headless says the coward word loses its first letter

parts.note: chicken as an adjective means cowardly, craven

explanation.surface: A bird running round like a headless chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' looks like the bird but means cowardly here.
explanation.definitionFit: This large black corvid is one example of a bird.

clue.text: Its effect in the sky gets no women excited?

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle over what celestial event fails to thrill women.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the lunar phase is something seen in the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The lunar phase when the disc is dark is a visible change overhead, the sky event here.

clue.text: Fall in ditch

definitions.meaning: to fall is to go down suddenly, a plunge
to ditch is to abandon or discard someone

explanation.surface: Someone tumbling into a trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditch' looks like a noun (a trench) but is a verb meaning abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fall in value and to abandon a friend or plan.

clue.text: Sponge made by winning team, unhappy with loaf

parts.note: a team that is ahead is said to be up
a side is a team
down means unhappy, low
a loaf of bread is a baked block, like a cake

explanation.surface: A cake baked by the victorious team, who are sad about the bread.
explanation.definitionFit: This dessert is a sponge baked over fruit and turned out inverted.

clue.text: Hate extremely delicate examination

indicators.note: extremely picks the letters at the extremes of delicate

parts.note: a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Loathing a very fiddly exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an intensifier for delicate but picks its end letters, D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something intensely is a direct synonym of hating it.

clue.text: Connoisseur's top bid for chest

indicators.note: in a down answer the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a bid is an offer at auction

explanation.surface: An expert's highest auction bid for an antique chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongbox for valuables is a kind of chest.

clue.text: T.S. Eliot wrong about leading edge of table knife

indicators.note: the scrambled poet letters go round the table letter, so about marks a container
wrong signals the letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: the poet's initials and surname supply the letters

indicators.note: the leading edge of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The poet T.S. Eliot fumbling with a table knife's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges TSELIOT to STILETO, around T from table. 'table knife' looks like one item; 'knife' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dagger with a narrow blade is a type of knife.

clue.text: Individual touring clubs long ago

indicators.note: the individual word travels round the clubs letter, so touring marks a container

parts.note: one means a single individual
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A single golfer who went round clubs years ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at some time in the past, formerly.

clue.text: Number collecting wood for burning

indicators.note: the number word gathers in the timber word, holding it inside

parts.note: one is a number
fir is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: Gathering firewood to burn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ablaze is literally burning.

clue.text: Admire Riviera terraced houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the run of letters is held within these words

explanation.surface: Admiring the terraced homes of the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' is the verb meaning holds, not the dwellings it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To think highly of someone, 'I really rate her', is to admire them.

clue.text: Forms an opinion on book

definitions.meaning: a book of the Old Testament following Joshua

explanation.surface: Someone forming a view about a book, like a reviewer.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means assesses; the Old Testament book narrates Israel's leaders before the kings.

clue.text: Musical item making racket — surefire winner, opening in Oliver!

parts.note: a racket is a swindle, a con
a cert is a certainty, a horse sure to win

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A number from the musical Oliver! that's a guaranteed noisy hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical' and 'Oliver!' point to the stage show, but the answer is a classical form.
explanation.definitionFit: A work for soloist and orchestra is one kind of piece in a musical programme.
